# Guest Designers

Hot Wheels has approached a number of celebrities or other notable individuals to design Hot Wheels cars. This article lists these individuals in an alphabetical order.

## Arushi Garg[]

[![ArushiGarg](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/e/e0/ArushiGarg.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/150?cb=20260604031159)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/e/e0/ArushiGarg.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20260604031159)
**Arushi Garg** is an American businesswoman based in Texas, working as a Brand Partnerships Manager for TikTok. She is the winner of the first season of *[Hot Wheels: Ultimate Challenge](/wiki/Hot_Wheels:_Ultimate_Challenge)* with her team, the *Carpoolers*. Garg also built and designed the *Jaipur Jewel* during the first season of Ultimate Challenge, making her advance to the final round and eventually winning the season.

### Designs[]

|---|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| [2024](/wiki/2024) | [Rally Resilience Nissan Skyline (R33)](/wiki/Rally_Resilience_Nissan_Skyline_(R33)) | [Mattel Creations Collaboratory](/wiki/Mattel_Creations_Collaboratory) | - | [Manson Cheung](/wiki/Manson_Cheung) | HYH22 | [![RallyResilience](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/4/4f/RallyResilience.jpg/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/100?cb=20240705085203)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/4/4f/RallyResilience.jpg/revision/latest?cb=20240705085203) |

## Chris Watson[]

[![ChrisWatson](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/e/e4/ChrisWatson.png/revision/latest/scale-to-width-down/150?cb=20260608030522)](https://static.wikia.nocookie.net/hotwheels/images/e/e4/ChrisWatson.png/revision/latest?cb=20260608030522)
**Chris Watson** is an New Zealand car builder. He is the winner of the [2023 Hot Wheels Legends Tour](/wiki/2023_Hot_Wheels_Legends_Tour) with his entrant, *[Chimera](/wiki/Mazda_MX-5_Miata_(2025))*, a custom [1990 Mazda MX-5 Miata](/wiki/Mazda_MX-5_Miata_(1991)) with significant Cyberpunk and Kaido Racer influence.

## Craig Meaux[]

**Craig Meaux** is an American hot rod builder. He is the winner of the [2022 Hot Wheels Legends Tour](/wiki/2022_Hot_Wheels_Legends_Tour) with his entrant, *[Texas Toot](/wiki/Mazda_Autozam)*, a custom [1992 Autozam Scrum](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Autozam_Scrum) monster truck with a 454 Chevrolet big block V8, large 30-inch wheels and train horns.

## Dale Earnhardt Jr.[]

**[Ralph Dale Earnhardt Jr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Earnhardt_Jr.)** (born 10 October 1974) is an American motorsports analyst and commentator, semi-retired professional stock car racing driver and team owner. The son of the late legendary stock car racing driver [Dale Earnhardt Sr.](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Dale_Earnhardt), Earnhardt raced from 1996 to 2017 full-time in various NASCAR series before calling time on his career. While Earnhardt has never been Cup Series Champion, he is a 15-time winner of NASCAR's Most Popular Driver award. He currently acts as an analyst and color commentator and competes in the NASCAR Xfinity Series on a part-time schedule for his own team, [JR Motorsports](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/JR_Motorsports).

## Danica Patrick[]

**[Danica Sue Patrick](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Danica_Patrick)** (born 25 March 1982) is an American retired professional open-wheel and stock car racing driver. Having raced in various different disciplines, Patrick started out in open-wheel racing, working from junior formulae to the IndyCar series; her win at the [2008 Indy Japan 300](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/2008_Indy_Japan_300) made her the only female driver to win an IndyCar race. Later in her career, she switched to NASCAR; this proved ill-fated, announcing that she would step away from racing full-time after 2017. She would make two more appearances at the 2018 Daytona 500 and 2018 Indianapolis 500 before retiring. Patrick has since become a television pundit; she has since courted controversy for some of her opinions on social media.

## Daniel Arsham[]

**[Daniel Lambert Arsham](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Daniel_Arsham)** (born 8 September 1980) is an American visual artist. Born in Cleveland, Ohio, Arsham is known for his "eroded" series of sculptures which depict people or objects with an "eroding" texture as they are being worn by the elements. He is based in New York City and has collaborated with numerous artists. Most of Arsham's works tend to feature white in them.

## Del Everitt[]

**Delmar Kenneth Everitt** (23 October 1933 – 28 January 1990) was an American toy designer. He was noted for his collaborations with toy designer Eddy Goldfarb and is known for having invented the [Farbs](/wiki/Farbs) and *Stompers* alongside him as well as a number of other toys. Goldfarb described him as "a car nut", having worked in Detroit. He passed away in January 1990.

## Eddy Goldfarb[]

**[Adolph Eddy Goldfarb](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eddy_Goldfarb)** (born 5 September 1921) is an American toy designer. The creator of over 800 toys, Goldfarb's better known creations include the *Yakity-Yak Talking Teeth*, *KerPlunk*, *Stompers*, *Battling Tops* and the *Vac-U-Form*. He was inducted into the Toy Industry Hall of Fame in 2003.

## Felipe Massa[]

**[Felipe Massa](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Felipe_Massa)** (born 25 April 1981) is a Brazilian professional racing driver. Initially starting out in karting, Massa worked his way up the motorsports ladder, eventually reaching Formula One. In Formula One, Massa would spend 15 seasons in F1 from 2002 to 2017 (with a sabbatical in 2003), racing for [Sauber](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sauber_Motorsport), [Ferrari](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Scuderia_Ferrari) and [Williams](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Williams_Grand_Prix_Engineering); his high point was in 2008, where he finished second in the Formula One world championship to [Lewis Hamilton](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lewis_Hamilton). Massa later moved to [Formula E](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Formula_E) after retiring from F1, spending two seasons with [Venturi](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Venturi_Racing). He currently competes in the [Stock Car Pro Series](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Stock_Car_Pro_Series).

## Shashank Shekhar[]

**Shashank Shekhar** is an Indian car designer. He is the winner of the 2024 Polestar Design Contest with his entrant, the [Polestar TRX](/wiki/Polestar_TRX), an extreme off-road vehicle with an angular appearance and Hot Wheels influence.

## Stephan Meyer-Metelmann[]

**Stephan Meyer-Metelmann** is a character artist, previously of Mainframe Entertainment, where he worked on a cancelled television series titled *[Hot Wheels: Stunt Strikers](/wiki/Stunt_Strikers)*. Two of his designs became [Hot Wheels](/wiki/Hot_Wheels) models through a [McDonald's](/wiki/McDonald%27s) promotion in [2007](/wiki/2007).

## Thomas Gilbert[]

**Thomas Gilbert** is a British automotive designer who acts as a Lead Exterior Designer of Aston Martin. Gilbert worked initially as an intern and a contract designer at Aston Martin before joining Rolls-Royce and Jaguar Land Rover, also on contracts; Gilbert joined Aston Martin full-time in 2019.

## Tony Hawk[]

**[Anthony Frank Hawk](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Tony_Hawk)** (born 12 May 1968) is an American professional skateboarder and entrepreneur. Widely acknowledged to be one of the sport's most influential skateboarders, Hawk is noted as a pioneer in modern vertical skateboarding. In 1999, Hawk became the first skateboarder to land a *900*; two-and-a-half mid-air rotations on a board. Hawk retired from professional competition in 2003 and now manages his company [Birdhouse Skateboards](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Birdhouse_Skateboards) as well as *[The Skatepark Foundation](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/The_Skatepark_Foundation)*. From 2020 to 2022, Hawk developed [a line of fingerboards](/wiki/Hot_Wheels_Skate) with Mattel.
